title: 33.5 A 224GHz 19.9% TR Varactor-Less VCO Utilizing a Multi-Section Switch-Loaded Coupled-Line Resonator
problem: THz and sub-THz circuits require tunable elements like voltage-controlled oscillators (VCOs) and passive phase shifters, but varactors suffer from low Q-factor at frequencies >100GHz with limited tuning range, while switched-capacitor banks suffer from high OFF-state capacitance and low Q-factor.
motivation: THz gas-phase spectroscopy, hyperspectral imaging, and high-speed communication demand silicon-based oscillators with tunable frequency, wide bandwidth, beamforming, and adequate power levels.
method: The oscillator tunes its frequency by using electronic switches to selectively activate inductors (magnetic coils) within a coupled-line resonator—a transmission line structure that naturally oscillates at specific frequencies. By switching different inductors in or out of the circuit, the resonant frequency shifts across a 19.9% range. This design replaces varactors (voltage-controlled capacitors), which perform poorly above 100GHz and suffer from low signal quality; the switched-inductor approach maintains high signal quality (Q-factor) throughout the tuning range at 224GHz.
key_novelty: Using electronically switchable inductors instead of varactors to tune a coupled-line resonator, enabling wide-range frequency tuning with high signal quality at sub-THz frequencies.
contributions: 224GHz sub-THz VCO with 19.9% tuning range (wide compared to varactor-limited ~5-10%)
Varactor-less design maintaining high Q-factor at sub-THz frequencies
Multi-section switch-loaded approach balancing tuning range and resonator quality
limitations: Phase noise, output power, and area/footprint not provided; comparison with other sub-THz VCO architectures absent.
